sentences.text: The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.)No.1948/2005 on the file of the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Thrissur is the appellant herein.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Thrissur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The respondents in the O.P. is the respondents herein.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in the accident that occurred on 02.07.2004.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal)

2. According to the petitioner, she was travelling as passenger in a minibus bearing Registration No.KL-9-KJ-9842 driven by the 2nd respondent along Thrissur - Palakkad National Highway, in a rash and negligent manner and hit on the backside of a lorry bearing Registration No.KA-05-AF-9977 which was parked by the side of the said road.
As a result of the accident, she sustained serious injuries.
The 1st respondent is the registered owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the minibus.
3. The 1st and 2nd respondents remained exparte.
The 3rd respondent/insurer filed a written statement, admitting the policy and disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the minibus.
The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of PW1 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A18.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.
5. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal quantified the compensation due to the petitioner as Rs.90490/-.
Thereafter, the Tribunal after disbelieving all the evidence adduced by the petitioner, awarded a token compensation of Rs.7,500/-.
6. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

7. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

8. Heard Sri.P.V.Chandramohan, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant, and Sri.S.K.Ajay Kumar, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
9.
The Point: In this case the accident and valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
The negligence on the part of the 2 nd respondent is also not disputed.
The petitioner has produced Ext.A2, copy of the charge sheet involved in the crime registered against the driver of the offending vehicle, in respect to the above accident.
In the light of the above charge sheet, MACA NO. 978 OF 2014 2025:KER:1841 negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle stands proved.

Therefore, the 3rd respondent, being the insurer, is liable to indemnify the compensation, which is Krishnakumari vs Duli Chand Lodha on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134995864/
2 liable to be awarded against the owner of the offending vehicle.
10.

sentences.text: The petitioner was aged 36 years on the date of the accident, on 02.07.2004.
According to the petitioner, she was a homemaker.

Since she could not prove her actual monthly income, her notional income is to be fixed as per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision of Ramachandrappa v. Manger, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13)
SCC 236].

entities.text:

SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, her notional income is fixed at Rs.4,500/.
11.
In the accident the petitioner sustained laceration left side of the face, left ear (pinna) and left side of leg.
Ext.A11 - discharge card shows fracture inferior pubic rami on right and lacerated wound on forehead and left ear (pinna).
It is unfortunate that the Tribunal has disbelieved Ext.A11 on the ground that, in Ext.A10 wound certificate there is no mention about any fracture.
The above finding of the Tribunal is unsustainable as it can be confirmed only when X-ray is taken.
The petitioner has produced Ext.A13 disability certificate and examined PW1, the Doctor who issued the same to prove the said certificate.
In Ext.A13 PW1 noticed mal united fracture of inferior pubic ramus with pain and restriction of movements of hip.
On the basis MACA NO. 978 OF 2014 2025:KER:1841 of the above findings the disability of the petitioner was fixed at 10%.
Though PW1 was cross-examined

,
nothing material could be brought out to discredit the above disability assessed by PW1.Therefore,
the disability of the petitioner as assessed by PW1 is accepted and fixed at 10%.

12. Since, on the date of accident, she was aged 36 years, 40 % of her income is to be added towards future prospects, and the multiplier to be applied is 15, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680].
13.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, compensation towards loss of disability will come to Rs.1,13,400/-.
14. Towards the head 'loss of earnings', the Tribunal has shown a sum of Rs.6000/- (3000x2 months).
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, she might have lost at least 3 months income.

Therefore, under the head 'loss of earnings' she is entitled to get a sum of Rs.13500/- (4500x3 months)
15.
Towards the heads 'extra nourishment' and 'transportation expenses' no compensation was awarded by the Tribunal.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, I hold that a compensation of Rs.5,000/- can be awarded on the head extra nourishment and Rs.2,000/- towards transportation expenses.
Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', no compensation was awarded by the Tribunal.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and the percentage of disability suffered by her, I hold that a compensation of Rs.50,000/- can be awarded on the head pain and suffering.

Krishnakumari vs Duli Chand Lodha on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134995864/
3 17.
Towards the head 'loss of amenities', no compensation was awarded by the Tribunal.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and the percentage of disability suffered by her, I hold that a compensation of Rs.25,000/- can be awarded on the head loss of amenities.
18. The petitioner has produced bills worth Rs.1,720/-.
Therefore, towards the head medical expenses a sum of Rs.1,720/- is awarded.
19. In the above circumstances, token compensation of Rs.7500/- awarded by the Tribunal will be deducted from the total amount awarded.
20. Therefore, the petitioner/ appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.2,10,620/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference.

Sl. Head of claim The amount given in  No. appeal (Rs.)
 1 Loss of earnings 13500
2 Transport to Hospital and back to home 2000  3
Extra nourishment 5000
MACA NO. 978 OF 2014  2025:KER:1841  4 Medical expenses 1720
5 Compensation for pain and suffering 50000  6 Compensation for continuing and 113400  permanent/partial disability
7 Loss of amenities 25000
Total 2,10,620  Amount enhanced 2,03,120 20.

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and the 3rd respondent is directed to deposit a total compensation of Rs.2,10,620/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Ten Thousand Six Hundred and Twenty Only),
less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest @ 8% per annum, from the date of the petition till realisation, excluding interest for a period of 66 days, the period of delay in filing the Krishnakumari vs Duli Chand Lodha on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134995864/
4 appeal, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
21. On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.

Sd/-
 C. PRATHEEP KUMAR,
